## Overview

::: {.summary}

📘 **HTML to JSX**
JSX is a **syntax extension for JavaScript** that lets us write HTML-like markup inside a component. It **looks like HTML but it is JavaScript**: Babel/Vite turn every tag into a function call (`React.createElement` / `jsx()`), and React renders real HTML elements into the DOM.

Because it is JavaScript, a few HTML habits must change: reserved words, camelCase names, functions instead of strings, objects instead of CSS strings, and every tag closed.

:::

---

## HTML vs JSX

JSX looks like HTML, but it is JavaScript, so a few things change:

| HTML                          | React JSX                               |
|-------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| `class="card"`                | `className="card"`                      |
| `for="name"`                  | `htmlFor="name"`                        |
| `onclick="doIt()"` (string)   | `onClick={doIt}` (a function)           |
| `onchange`, `onsubmit`        | `onChange`, `onSubmit` (camelCase)      |
| `style="color:red"`           | `style={{ color: "red" }}` (an object)  |
| `<br>`, `<img src="a.png">`   | `<br />`, `<img src="a.png" />`         |
| `return false` / `preventDefault()` | always `event.preventDefault()`   |

: HTML vs JSX {.striped .hover}

::: {.callout-tip}
## Pass the function, don't call it
`onClick={handleClick}` ✅ passes the function and React calls it on click.
`onClick={handleClick()}` ❌ calls it immediately on every render.
If you need arguments, wrap it: `onClick={() => handleClick(id)}`.
:::

## `className` and `htmlFor`

`class` and `for` are **reserved words** in JavaScript (`class Person {}`, `for (...)`), so JSX uses the DOM property names instead:

``` {.jsx .code-overflow-wrap filename="Field.jsx"}
<div className="field">
  <label htmlFor="email">Email</label>
  <input id="email" type="email" className="input" />
</div>
```

The browser still receives `class="field"` and `for="email"`.

## Events: camelCase and functions

| HTML                                  | JSX                                    |
|---------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| `<button onclick="save()">`           | `<button onClick={save}>`              |
| `<input onchange="check(this)">`      | `<input onChange={(e) => check(e.target)} />` |
| `<form onsubmit="return send()">`     | `<form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>`       |
| `<div onmouseover="...">`             | `<div onMouseOver={...}>`              |

- Event names are **camelCase**: `onClick`, `onChange`, `onSubmit`, `onKeyDown`, `onMouseOver`.
- The value is a **function** between curly braces, not a string of code.
- `return false` does not cancel anything in React: call `event.preventDefault()`.
- In React `onChange` fires **on every keystroke** (like the HTML `input` event).

## The `style` attribute is an object

In HTML `style` is a CSS string. In JSX it is a **JavaScript object** with **camelCase** property names:

``` {.jsx .code-overflow-wrap filename="Badge.jsx"}
// HTML: <span style="background-color: gold; font-size: 14px">New</span>

const badgeStyle = { backgroundColor: "gold", fontSize: 14, padding: "2px 6px" };

export default function Badge() {
  return <span style={badgeStyle}>New</span>;
}

// or inline: the outer braces are JSX, the inner braces are the object
<span style={{ backgroundColor: "gold", fontSize: 14 }}>New</span>
```

Numbers without units are treated as `px` (`fontSize: 14` → `14px`). For most styling, prefer CSS classes: see [CSS basics for React](/reactjs/reactjs-what-html-css.qmd).

## Close every tag

HTML forgives `<br>`, `<img>`, `<input>`, `<hr>` and even an unclosed `<li>`. JSX doesn't:

``` {.jsx .code-overflow-wrap filename="Profile.jsx"}
<img src="/avatar.png" alt="Avatar" />
<br />
<input type="text" />
<MyComponent />          {/* components can self-close too */}
```

## One root element and fragments

A component must **return a single root element**. If you don't want an extra `<div>` in the DOM, use a **fragment** `<>...</>`:

``` {.jsx .code-overflow-wrap filename="Header.jsx"}
export default function Header() {
  return (
    <>
      <h1>My shop</h1>
      <nav>
        <a href="/">Home</a>
      </nav>
    </>
  );
}
```

When you render a list of fragments with `map()`, use the long form so you can pass a `key`: `<Fragment key={item.id}>...</Fragment>`.

## JavaScript in curly braces

Inside JSX, `{ }` opens a window to JavaScript: variables, expressions, function calls, `map()`, ternaries.

``` {.jsx .code-overflow-wrap filename="List.jsx"}
const user = { name: "Ada", avatar: "/ada.png" };
const items = ["HTML", "CSS", "JS"];

<div>
  <h2>Hello {user.name}</h2>
  <img src={user.avatar} alt={user.name} />
  <ul>
    {items.map((item) => <li key={item}>{item}</li>)}
  </ul>
  {items.length > 2 ? <p>Busy week!</p> : <p>Easy week</p>}
</div>
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Comments in JSX
HTML comments `<!-- -->` don't work in JSX. Use `{/* comment */}`.
:::

## Full example: a signup form

The signup form from [HTML forms](/reactjs/reactjs-what-html-forms.qmd), now as a React component with state and events:

``` {.jsx .code-overflow-wrap filename="SignupForm.jsx"}
import { useState } from "react";

export default function SignupForm() {
  const [name, setName] = useState("");
  const [message, setMessage] = useState("");

  function handleSubmit(event) {
    event.preventDefault();               // same as in plain JS: no page reload
    setMessage(`Welcome, ${name}!`);
  }

  return (
    <form className="signup" onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
      <label htmlFor="name">Name</label>
      <input
        id="name"
        type="text"
        value={name}
        onChange={(event) => setName(event.target.value)}
      />

      <button type="submit" onMouseOver={() => console.log("hover")}>
        Send
      </button>

      {message && <p>{message}</p>}
    </form>
  );
}
```

- `onSubmit`, `onChange` and `onMouseOver` are the same DOM events, written in **camelCase** and receiving a **function**.
- The handler receives an **event object** (React wraps the native one in a *SyntheticEvent* with the same API: `target`, `key`, `preventDefault()`, `stopPropagation()`).
- In React `onChange` fires **on every keystroke**, like the HTML `input` event.
- We don't use `getElementById` or `addEventListener`: React updates the DOM for us when the **state** changes.

More about JSX in [React JS: JSX](/reactjs/reactjs-what-jsx.qmd), about components in [React JS: Components](/reactjs/reactjs-what-components.qmd) and about state in [React JS: useState](/reactjs/reactjs-hook-state.qmd).
